transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Cho, Jules Nguyen (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Samir Desai, Priya Kapoor, Oliver Reed (Acme)
Recording link: (redacted)

[00:00] Maya Patel: okay everyone good morning thanks for joining the weekly POC sync, uh quick roll call and then we'll go through onboarding status and the short results we ran last week.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: hey Maya, here. Samir and Priya are on.
[00:21] Samir Desai: yep here.
[00:23] Priya Kapoor: here, thanks.
[00:25] Maya Patel: great, Ethan you wanna kick off with infra readiness?
[00:30] Ethan Cho: yeah sure, so quick recap — last week we validated the model pull and basic inference in the dev VPC. We saw... um a couple of networking hiccups, mostly around IP allowlist and the NAT gateway timing out when the peering was tested. Samir updated a rule but we still need the static egress IP from your side for final allowlist.
[00:51] Samir Desai: right, we have a list of public egress IPs — I can share. I think the missing bit was the route table association for the peering. I fixed most of that yesterday. Also on the service account, we created the token but need the permissions scoped for the S3 bucket.
[01:10] Ethan Cho: perfect — for the benchmark we'll need a short-lived service account with read access to the test dataset and ability to call the Redwood endpoint. If you can also add the CIDR for the dedicated subnets that would help.
[01:25] Lena Ortiz: yep I'll have Samir share the details right after. We're planning to use a 100k sample of redacted customer logs for quality tests. Is that okay?
[01:33] Maya Patel: redacted is perfect; thanks. We prefer a representative sample but no PII.
[01:38] Oliver Reed: small note — we saw some hallucinations on edge cases in the first run, probably prompt tuning needed. We'll include a flagged set.
[01:46] Ethan Cho: noted. Regarding results — quick preview: we ran a 500 request test in our dev env using a 8k context window, and with KV cache enabled we saw median latency around 120ms per request (this is token generation time only), p95 around 420ms. Cost per 1k tokens was roughly $X. The customer environment will vary, but the important part is the delta when KV cache is disabled — latency increased ~2.8x.
[02:12] Lena Ortiz: can you clarify what you mean by KV cache? is that the prefix cache or the full KV?
[02:16] Ethan Cho: yeah good call — it's the KV cache used for prefix reuse across calls, basically reduces redundant recomputation of earlier layers/kv. It's not a long-term datastore.
[02:27] Priya Kapoor: on security — I need to review key management. Are you using KMS? How do we rotate keys and where do logs live? We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:38] Maya Patel: yes we support KMS integration, and for Private deployments keys can be customer-managed HSM. We'll send our SOC2 and the KMS integration docs in the post-call packet. Audit logs can be forwarded — we'll include the retention options and sample log layout.
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: thanks, also about data residency — we need to confirm that the test data stays in the EU region if we move to that environment.
[03:00] Maya Patel: noted — we have region pinning for models and data. We'll include region-residency matrix.
[03:06] Jules Nguyen: quick operational note from CS — onboarding checklist progress: account created, dev cluster connected, basic inference validated, outstanding items: VPC peering confirmation, service account perms, and security questionnaire.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: that sounds right.
[03:22] Maya Patel: ok let's go through a short timeline for next week — Ethan will run a 2k request benchmark with KV cache on and off, and with batching at two settings (batch 4 and batch 8) to show cost/latency tradeoffs. Ethan, does that work?
[03:36] Ethan Cho: yeah I'll run the following matrix: KV on/off x batching 1/4/8 x quantization level default vs q4_0 (just to show perf differences). I'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost per call.
[03:50] Samir Desai: do you have a preferred load generator? We can use locust or the Redwood harness.
[03:55] Ethan Cho: Redwood harness is fine — it's what produced the earlier numbers. If you prefer locust, we can adapt.
[04:01] Oliver Reed: also include a small cold-start test please, to see the first-request penalty when KV miss.
[04:06] Ethan Cho: good call.
[04:08] Maya Patel: while Ethan runs that, we'll polish the prompt set and share a curated eval set to track quality regressions. Oliver, can you pick top 50 edge-case prompts?
[04:18] Oliver Reed: yep I'll do that and send by Tues.
[04:21] Priya Kapoor: on compliance items — can you confirm retention defaults and ability to opt out of persisting cache/content? We may need to ensure logs are ephemeral for POC.
[04:32] Maya Patel: retention can be configured; for POC we can set short retention and disable persistent KV storage if required. We'll note that in the onboarding doc.
[04:40] Samir Desai: I have a question about private deployment vs dedicated. For us cost vs latency is a tradeoff; how do you recommend we choose?
[04:49] Maya Patel: good question — typically Dedicated gives you predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools, lower unit cost at scale. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives maximum control for compliance but higher ops overhead. For a POC we recommend starting with Dedicated or Hosted in a customer region and then if compliance requires, pivot to Private. We'll share a short decision matrix.
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: do you have SLAs for p95 latency on dedicated?
[05:13] Ethan Cho: we have latency targets and SLA tiers depending on commit; we'll include typical p95 numbers for similar customers in the packet.
[05:20] Maya Patel: quick note — competitor question: Anthropic came up in our last thread. Their safety model is strong but our differentiation is operational: cost controls, rollouts, and KV/cache optimizations that reduce token spend.
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: okay, please include a short comparison note.
[05:36] Maya Patel: will do.
[05:38] [09:00] (background cross-talk)
[05:40] Ethan Cho: okay moving to a short demo of the test harness logs — I'll paste a snippet here in the chat, but tl;dr: with KV cache, identical prompts reused showed 70-80% token savings on repeated contexts and stable latencies. Without KV we saw more variance.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: that token savings is interesting — can you show cost normalized per 1k unique tokens so we can compare to our internal numbers?
[06:06] Ethan Cho: yes I'll normalize and include in the benchmark sheet.
[06:10] Oliver Reed: another quality note — model variant selection is important. Can you run a quick A/B of model v1.6 vs v1.7? We saw quality delta in our last run.
[06:20] Ethan Cho: I can include that as a tie-breaker but it will add runs; I'll do it for the primary prompt set only.
[06:26] Maya Patel: great.
[06:28] Priya Kapoor: one more on security — SIEM integration: do you support syslog or S3 log push? We need near real-time.
[06:37] Maya Patel: we can forward logs to S3, syslog, or stream to your SIEM via our ingestion pipeline. We'll include sample configuration for each.
[06:46] Samir Desai: okay I'll coordinate with our security team once we get the doc.
[06:50] Jules Nguyen: ops question — who will own the fallout if we hit rate limits in Dedicated vs Hosted? We need to understand throttling behavior.
[07:00] Ethan Cho: Redwood enforces per-route quotas and has tiered backpressure; for Dedicated we can bump capacity or have burst pools. We'll document behavior and propose a fallback policy (downgrade to smaller model or queue).
[07:14] Maya Patel: let's capture that as an action item — propose fallback policy for the POC.
[07:19] Lena Ortiz: sounds good.
[07:22] Maya Patel: any other blockers?
[07:24] Samir Desai: just the service account perms and IP allowlist. Once that's done I can run a sanity traffic test.
[07:30] Oliver Reed: nothing else, we just need the eval set from Redwood.
[07:33] Maya Patel: we'll share the eval/prompt template and the SOC2 + network diagram after this call. Ethan will run the benchmark and we reconvene next week to review the results and schedule the security deep dive.
[07:45] Priya Kapoor: thanks, can we tentatively schedule the security deep dive for Wed Feb 12?
[07:50] Maya Patel: I'll check with Redwood security and propose times.
[07:53] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[08:00] Maya Patel: ok great thanks all, we'll follow up in email with docs and the action items. Bye.
[44:30] (call ended)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words and timestamps are approximate. References shared in chat: soc2_report.pdf (link), onboarding_checklist.xlsx (link), benchmark_template.csv (link).
